title: FlashVector: Agent for Hierarchical Model Serving Stack Optimization
scope: Reread all nine physical PDF pages including references to correct comparison coverage, with visual inspection of Algorithm 1 and Tables 3/4. No GPU execution, code audit or independent reproduction.
publication_identity: Author arXiv preprint v1 dated 2026-09-15; conference publication identity not verified.
method: Page-preserving PDFKit text, complete reread, with visual checks. Findings paraphrased; each 1-based inclusive source-line block is pinned by SHA-256 after joining lines with a terminal newline.

observations.finding: Pinned author arXiv v1 dated 2026-09-15, Stanford/Unity, nine physical pages. Optimizes production recommender serving at Unity Vector, across GPU kernels, framework graphs, NVIDIA Triton model server and feature processing.

A common layer-specific Profile/Diagnose/Optimize/Verify interface plus post-run Refine. Algorithm 1 randomly samples one layer per iteration, ranks that layer's own hypotheses and tests a candidate; local acceptance is followed by full-stack validation.

Verification preserves recorded model inputs/outputs, with change-specific equality/numeric/business checks. Repeated no-op runs estimate a stated ±6% end-to-end noise floor; 2–6% gains use up to 8x samples. Locally passing changes can be rejected by full-stack load tests.

Refine updates the knowledge base after the loop. New model releases and sufficiently old analyses retrigger optimization without manual invocation; both accepted and rejected history inform subsequent runs.

Table 1 model-server outcomes reach 2x throughput and 1.98x latency speedup; 30x is a serialization-step result, 3.56x an attention-module result. Feature-pod throughput grows 940 to about 1500 RPS at fixed latency SLO, about 1.6x, through sequential combined changes.

Current configuration sweep varies instance count and dynamic batch size; queue policy is derived from SLO rather than searched. Replica count is autoscaler-managed. More than 2x variation across trials is not a measured 2x gain over the baseline for every model.

Trials replay actual production requests on an isolated node of the production machine type, including captured preprocessor outputs for two-stage models. Optimize opens a PR; Verify uses a shadow-traffic canary before adopting or discarding it. The loop repeats at the next model release.

Visual inspection confirms Model B SLO 250 ms but chosen-trial p99 271 ms. Table caption describes throughput sustained at the SLO; do not claim all four rows independently demonstrate satisfying their stated SLO.

Isolated-node experiments, production replay, automatic retriggering, code/configuration changes and canary adoption already have explicit coverage. This paper's recommender workload does not itself establish a specific LLM PD router/KV-session replacement mechanism.

interpretation_limits: Opening a PR, modifying runtime configuration and being continuously triggered do not establish in-place engine hot-swap.
The documented sweep currently searches two parameters; distinguish these from other supported levers and SLO-derived queue policy.
Model-server, serialization-step, attention-module and feature-pod speedups have different denominators.
Table 4 Model B has a literal p99/SLO mismatch. Preserve values rather than silently correcting or treating all configurations as SLO compliant.
Absence of LLM PD replacement detail in this paper does not establish absence in unpublished implementation.
